title: John Chrysostom on Job 1:21
body: “What if thou art come to great dignity, and hast at any time obtained some office of Church government? Be not high-minded.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
bodyEs: “¿Y si has llegado a gran dignidad y has obtenido alguna vez algún oficio de gobierno en la Iglesia? No te ensoberbezcas.”

title: John Chrysostom on Job 1:21
body: “Seest thou how he bears himself along into speaking of the Son? For if "we give thanks with much joy," it is a great thing that is spoken of.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon
bodyEs: “¿Ves cómo se lanza a hablar del Hijo? Porque si "damos gracias con mucho gozo", es una gran cosa de la que se habla.”

title: John Chrysostom on Job 2:6
body: “And he said not simply, "That the spirit may be saved," but "in that day." Well and seasonably doth he remind them of that day in order that both they might more readily apply themselves to the cure, and that the person censured might the rather receive his words, not as it were of anger, but as the forethought of an anxious father.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
bodyEs: “Y no dijo simplemente: "el espíritu sea salvo", sino "en el día del Señor Jesús". Bien y a tiempo les recuerda aquel día, para que tanto ellos se aplicaran con más prontitud a la cura, como para que la persona censurada recibiera sus palabras más bien, no como de enojo, sino como la previsión de un padre angustiado.”

title: John Chrysostom on Job 2:9
body: “What means, "Lest by any means the tempter had tempted you"? Dost thou see that to be shaken in afflictions proceeds from the devil, and from his seduction?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon
bodyEs: “¿Qué significa: "no sea que os haya tentado el tentador"? ¿Ves que el ser sacudido en las aflicciones procede del diablo y de su seducción?”

title: John Chrysostom on Job 2:9
body: “For tell me when dost thou account Job blessed? When he had so many camels, and flocks, and herds, or when he uttered that saying: "The Lord gave, the Lord hath taken away"?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews
bodyEs: “Porque dime: ¿cuándo cuentas bienaventurado a Job? ¿Cuando tenía tantos camellos, y rebaños, y ganados, o cuando pronunció aquella sentencia: "Jehová dió, y Jehová quitó"?”

title: John Chrysostom on Job 5:13
body: “And he is not content with his own arguments, but he has also adduced testimony again, saying, "For it is written, (Job v.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on the Epistles to the Corinthians
bodyEs: “Y no se contenta con sus propios argumentos, sino que también ha aducido de nuevo un testimonio, diciendo: "Porque escrito está, (Job 5.”

title: John Chrysostom on Job 9:8
body: “The Jews under the guidance of Moses passed over the Red Sea, but that case is widely different from this. He did all with prayer and as a servant, but Christ with absolute power.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on John and Hebrews
bodyEs: “Los judíos, bajo la guía de Moisés, pasaron el mar Rojo, pero aquel caso es muy distinto de este. Él lo hizo todo con oración y como siervo, pero Cristo con poder absoluto.”

title: John Chrysostom on Job 38:3
body: “Moral. Let not any one of them that eat this Passover look towards Egypt, but towards Heaven, towards "Jerusalem that is above." (Gal.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Galatians through Philemon
bodyEs: “Moraleja. Ninguno de los que comen esta Pascua mire hacia Egipto, sino hacia el cielo, hacia "la Jerusalem de arriba." (Gál.”
